0102.text: Wagner's The Flying Dutchman premieres in Dresden.

0105.text: The Palais Garnier, one of the most famous opera houses in the world, is inaugurated in Paris.

0107.text: Marian Anderson became the first African-American to perform with the Metropolitan Opera in New York.

0108.text: George Frideric Handel's opera Ariodante premiered at the Covent Garden Theatre in London.

0114.text: Ravel's Piano Concerto in G premieres in Paris with Marguerite Long.
Giacomo Puccini's opera Tosca, based on the play La Tosca by French dramatist Victorien Sardou, premiered at the Teatro Costanzi in Rome.

0115.text: Tchaikovsky's The Sleeping Beauty premieres at the Mariinsky Theatre.

0119.text: Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il trovatore receives its premiere performance in Rome.

0125.text: Richard Strauss's opera Elektra receives its debut performance at the Dresden State Opera.

0126.text: Richard Strauss's Der Rosenkavalier premieres in Dresden.
Mozart's Così fan tutte premieres in Vienna.

0127.text: Modest Mussorgsky's opera Boris Godunov premieres in Mariinsky Theatre in St.Petersburg.

0201.text: Puccini's Manon Lescaut premieres in Turin.
Giacomo Puccini's opera La bohème premiered at the Teatro Regio in Turin, Italy, eventually becoming one of the most frequently performed operas internationally.

0205.text: Verdi's Otello premieres at La Scala, Milan.
Claudio Monteverdi's last opera, L'incoronazione di Poppea, was performed theatrically for the first time in more than 250 years.

0209.text: Verdi's last opera, Falstaff, premieres at La Scala, Milan.

0211.text: Anton Bruckner's 9th Symphony receives its first performance in Vienna, Austria.
Giuseppe Verdi's opera I Lombardi alla prima crociata receives its first performance in Milan, Italy.
Gaetano Donizetti's opera La fille du régiment receives its first performance in Paris, France.

0212.text: Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue premieres at Aeolian Hall, New York.

0217.text: Italian composer Giacomo Puccini's Madama Butterfly  premiered at La Scala in Milan to poor reviews, forcing him to revise the opera.

0218.text: Brahms's complete German Requiem premieres in Leipzig.
The ballad opera called Flora, or Hob in the Well went down in history as the first opera of any kind to be produced in North America (Charleston, S.C.)

0220.text: The Barber of Seville, an opera buffa composed by Gioachino Rossini, premiered at the Teatro Argentina in Rome to jeers from the audience.
Tchaikovsky's ballet Swan Lake receives its premiere at the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow.

0224.text: Grieg's Peer Gynt music premieres in Christiania (Oslo).
George Frideric Handel's Rinaldo, the first Italian-language opera written specifically for the London stage, premiered.
Italian composer Claudio Monteverdi's L'Orfeo, considered the first fully developed opera, premiered in Mantua.

0225.text: George Frideric Handel's opera Nero premiered in Hamburg.

0226.text: In the first significant cultural visit from the United States to North Korea since the Korean War, the New York Philharmonic Orchestra performed in Pyongyang.

0227.text: The D'Oyly Carte Opera Company, known for its performances of Gilbert and Sullivan's Savoy operas, gave its final performance.

0303.text: Bizet's Carmen premieres at the Opéra-Comique in Paris.

0305.text: Mefistofele, an opera by Arrigo Boito, receives its premiere performance at La Scala.

0306.text: Giuseppe Verdi's La traviata premiered at La Fenice in Venice, but the performance was considered so bad that it caused him to revise portions of the opera.

0309.text: Nabucco, an opera by Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi that established his reputation, premiered at La Scala in Milan.

0311.text: Verdi's Rigoletto premieres at La Fenice in Venice.
Mendelssohn revives Bach's St Matthew Passion in Berlin.

0312.text: Copland's Fanfare for the Common Man premieres in Cincinnati.

0313.text: German composer Felix Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto was premiered in Leipzig with Ferdinand David as the soloist.

0314.text: The Mikado, Gilbert and Sullivan's most frequently performed Savoy opera, debuted at the Savoy Theatre in London.
The Petite messe solennelle by Gioachino Rossini was first performed in Paris, 34 years after his retirement as a composer.

0318.text: The premiere of William Henry Fry's Leonora in Philadelphia is the first known performance of a grand opera by an American composer.

0319.text: Haydn's The Creation has its first public performance in Vienna.
Dvořák's Cello Concerto premieres in London.
The secular oratorio A Child of Our Time by Michael Tippett premiered at the Adelphi Theatre in London.

0321.text: Schubert's 'Great' C major Symphony premieres in Leipzig under Mendelssohn.
Ravel's opera L'enfant et les sortilèges, to a libretto by Colette, is premiered at the Opéra de Monte-Carlo.

0324.text: Johann Sebastian Bach dedicates six concertos to Margrave Christian Ludwig of Brandenburg-Schwedt, now commonly called the Brandenburg Concertos, BWV 1046–1051.

0328.text: First concert of the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Otto Nicolai.

0329.text: Tchaikovsky's Eugene Onegin premieres in Moscow, sung by students.

0331.text: Rusalka by Antonín Dvořák premieres at the National Opera House in Prague.

0401.text: J. S. Bach's later Easter Oratorio in its first version is performed at the Nikolaikirche in Leipzig on Easter Sunday.

0402.text: Ludwig van Beethoven leads the premiere of his First Symphony in Vienna.

0405.text: Johann Strauss II's Die Fledermaus premieres in Vienna.

0407.text: German composer Ludwig van Beethoven premieres his Third Symphony, at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna.

0409.text: Marian Anderson sings at the Lincoln Memorial to 75,000 people.

0413.text: The first performance of the oratorio Messiah by George Frideric Handel took place in Dublin.

0415.text: Serse, an opera by Baroque composer George Frideric Handel loosely based on Xerxes I of Persia, premiered in London.

0420.text: Vladimir Horowitz plays in Moscow, his first concert there in 61 years.

0424.text: German composer Max Bruch conducted the premiere of his first violin concerto.

0425.text: Puccini's Turandot premieres at La Scala, conducted by Toscanini.

0427.text: Handel's Music for the Royal Fireworks is performed in Green Park, London.

0428.text: Igor Stravinsky conducts the premiere of his American ballet, Orpheus at the New York City Center.

0430.text: Debussy's Pelléas et Mélisande premieres in Paris.

0501.text: The Marriage of Figaro, an opera buffa by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, premiered at the Burgtheater in Vienna.

0502.text: Prokofiev's Peter and the Wolf premieres in Moscow.

0505.text: Carnegie Hall in New York City, built by the philanthropist Andrew Carnegie, officially opened with a concert conducted by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky.

0507.text: World premiere of Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony in Vienna, Austria. The performance is conducted by Michael Umlauf under the composer's supervision.

0509.text: Vladimir Horowitz returns to Carnegie Hall after 12 years away.

0516.text: The first modern performance of Claudio Monteverdi's opera Il ritorno d'Ulisse in patria occurred in Paris.

0517.text: The opera Cavalleria rusticana by Pietro Mascagni, premieres at the Teatro Costanzi in Rome, beginning the verismo period in Italian opera.

0521.text: The opera Doktor Faust, unfinished when composer Ferruccio Busoni died, was premiered in Dresden.

0522.text: Giuseppe Verdi's Requiem was first performed in the San Marco church in Milan to commemorate the first anniversary of Alessandro Manzoni's death.

0525.text: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera H.M.S. Pinafore (poster featured) premiered at the Opera Comique in London.

0528.text: Italian composer Claudio Monteverdi debuted his second opera L'Arianna, now one of his lost works, at a royal wedding in Mantua.

0530.text: Bedřich Smetana's comic opera The Bartered Bride premiered in Prague.

0607.text: Britten's Peter Grimes premieres at Sadler's Wells, London.

0608.text: Orff's Carmina Burana premieres in Frankfurt.
Ravel's Daphnis et Chloé premieres in Paris.

0610.text: Wagner's Tristan und Isolde premieres in Munich.

0613.text: Twentieth opera of Giuseppe Verdi, Les vêpres siciliennes ("The Sicilian Vespers"), is premiered in Paris.

0614.text: Vaughan Williams's The Lark Ascending premieres in its orchestral version.

0618.text: Weber's Der Freischütz premieres in Berlin.
English composer Benjamin Britten's one-act opera Noye's Fludde was premiered at the Aldeburgh Festival.

0619.text: Elgar's Enigma Variations premieres in London.
King Roger, an opera about Roger II of Sicily by Karol Szymanowski,  was premiered at the Grand Theatre in Warsaw.

0621.text: Wagner's Die Meistersinger premieres in Munich.

0626.text: Wagner's Die Walküre premieres in Munich.

0628.text: Giselle, a ballet by the French composer Adolphe Adam, was first performed at the Théâtre de l'Académie Royale de Musique in Paris.

0702.text: Sibelius's Finlandia is performed in its final form in Helsinki.

0711.text: The Hollywood Bowl opens its first season.

0716.text: Max Reger's Hebbel Requiem was first performed in a memorial concert for the composer, conducted by Philipp Wolfrum.
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's opera Die Entführung aus dem Serail premiered in Vienna, after which Emperor Joseph II anecdotally remarked that it had "too many notes".

0717.text: Handel's Water Music is first played on the Thames for King George I.

0725.text: Mozart completed his Symphony No. 40, one of his two extant symphonies in a minor key.

0726.text: Premiere of Richard Wagner's opera Parsifal at Bayreuth.

0803.text: Rossini's William Tell premieres in Paris.
The theatre La Scala in Milan is inaugurated with the première of Antonio Salieri's Europa riconosciuta.

0809.text: Shostakovich's Symphony No. 7 was premiered in Leningrad while the city was under siege by Nazi forces.

0813.text: A performance of Das Rheingold opened the first performance of Richard Wagner's Ring cycle at the inaugural Bayreuth Festival, attended by emperors and other composers.

0816.text: Richard Wagner's Siegfried, the penultimate opera in his Ring cycle, is premiered at the Bayreuth Festspielhaus.

0817.text: Richard Wagner's Götterdämmerung, the last opera in his Ring cycle, premieres at the Bayreuth Festspielhaus.

0828.text: Wagner's Lohengrin premieres in Weimar, conducted by Liszt.

0829.text: American experimental composer John Cage's 4’33” premieres at Maverick Concert Hall, played by American pianist David Tudor.

0908.text: The Kennedy Center opens with Bernstein's Mass.

0912.text: Gustav Mahler's Symphony No. 8, one of the largest-scale choral works in the classical concert repertoire and popularly known as the "Symphony of a Thousand", was first performed in Munich.

0914.text: George Frideric Handel completes his oratorio Messiah.

0916.text: Felix Mendelssohn completed the score of his Violin Concerto, his final concerto.
The Metropolitan Opera House opens at Lincoln Center in New York City with the world premiere of Samuel Barber's opera Antony and Cleopatra.

0918.text: The Royal Opera House in Covent Garden, London, opens.

0922.text: Das Rheingold, the first of four operas in Der Ring des Nibelungen by the German composer Richard Wagner, was first performed in Munich.

0923.text: Philharmonic Hall, the first Lincoln Center building, opens.

0926.text: Donizetti's Lucia di Lammermoor premieres in Naples.

0929.text: Holst's The Planets is first performed, privately, at Queen's Hall, London.

0930.text: Georges Bizet's opera Les pêcheurs de perles premiered at the Théâtre Lyrique in Paris.
Mozart conducted the premiere of his last opera, The Magic Flute, in Vienna.

1006.text: Euridice, the earliest surviving opera, receives its première performance, beginning the Baroque period.

1010.text: Gershwin's Porgy and Bess opens on Broadway at the Alvin Theatre.

1014.text: Mendelssohn's Midsummer Night's Dream music premieres in Potsdam.

1015.text: Debussy's La mer premieres in Paris.

1016.text: Copland's Rodeo premieres in New York.
The Chicago Symphony Orchestra gives its first concert.
Háry János, a Hungarian folk opera by Zoltán Kodály, was premiered at the Royal Hungarian Opera House in Budapest.

1017.text: Ascanio in Alba, an opera composed by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart at the age of 15, premiered in Milan.

1018.text: Johannes Brahms conducted the premiere of his Double Concerto, composed for violinist Joseph Joachim and cellist Robert Hausmann.

1019.text: Elgar's Pomp and Circumstance March No. 1 premieres in Liverpool.

1020.text: The Sydney Opera House is opened by Elizabeth II after 14 years of construction.

1021.text: French composer Jacques Offenbach's operetta Orpheus in the Underworld, featuring the music most associated with the can-can, was first performed at the Théâtre des Bouffes-Parisiens in Paris.

1022.text: The Boston Symphony Orchestra gives its first concert.
John Adams' opera Nixon in China premiered.
The Metropolitan Opera House in New York City opens with a performance of Charles Gounod's Faust.

1025.text: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's Piano Concerto No. 1 in B♭ minor, Op. 23 premieres in Boston, Massachusetts, with Benjamin Johnson Lang as conductor and Hans von Bülow as soloist.

1028.text: Pyotr Tchaikovsky's Symphony No. 6 in B Minor, Pathétique receives its première performance only nine days before the composer's death.

1029.text: Mozart's Don Giovanni premieres in Prague.

1030.text: Copland's Appalachian Spring premieres at the Library of Congress.

1104.text: Brahms's First Symphony premieres in Karlsruhe.
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's Symphony No. 36 is performed for the first time in Linz, Austria.
The Teatro di San Carlo, the oldest working opera house in Europe, is inaugurated in Naples, Italy.

1105.text: Barber's Adagio for Strings premieres on NBC radio under Toscanini.
After being destroyed in World War II, the rebuilt Vienna State Opera reopens with a performance of Beethoven's Fidelio.

1107.text: Rachmaninoff's Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini premieres in Baltimore.

1109.text: Rachmaninoff's Second Piano Concerto premieres in full in Moscow.

1114.text: Leonard Bernstein, 25, makes his surprise debut leading the New York Philharmonic.

1116.text: The Philadelphia Orchestra gives its first concert.

1120.text: Beethoven's only opera, Fidelio, premieres in Vienna.

1122.text: Ravel's Boléro premieres at the Paris Opéra, danced by Ida Rubinstein.

1125.text: Gustav Mahler's Symphony No. 4 premiered in Munich.

1128.text: Rachmaninoff's Third Piano Concerto premieres in New York.
Beethoven's Piano Concerto No. 5 premiered at the Gewandhaus in Leipzig.

1203.text: Gershwin's Concerto in F premieres at Carnegie Hall.

1204.text: Tchaikovsky's Violin Concerto premieres in Vienna with Adolph Brodsky.

1205.text: Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique premieres in Paris.
New Haven Symphony Orchestra of Connecticut performs its first concert.

1207.text: First concert of the New York Philharmonic, founded by Ureli Corelli Hill.
The Royal Opera House opens at Covent Garden, London, England.

1208.text: Beethoven's Seventh Symphony premieres in Vienna.

1209.text: Richard Strauss's Salome premieres in Dresden.

1210.text: Puccini's La fanciulla del West premieres at the Met.

1213.text: Mahler's Second Symphony, 'Resurrection', premieres in Berlin.
An American in Paris, a jazz-influenced orchestral piece by George Gershwin, premiered at Carnegie Hall in New York.

1214.text: Wozzeck by composer Alban Berg, described as the first atonal opera, premiered at the Berlin State Opera.
Giacomo Puccini's comic opera Gianni Schicchi premiered at the Metropolitan Opera in New York City.

1215.text: Symphony No. 9 ("From the New World" a.k.a. the "New World Symphony") by Antonín Dvořák premieres in a public afternoon rehearsal at Carnegie Hall in New York City, followed by a concert premiere on the evening of December 16.

1216.text: Czech composer Antonín Dvořák's New World Symphony premiered at Carnegie Hall in New York City.

1217.text: First performance of the Unfinished Symphony by Franz Schubert.

1218.text: Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker premieres at the Mariinsky Theatre in St Petersburg.

1222.text: Debussy's Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun premieres in Paris.
Ludwig van Beethoven conducts and performs in concert at the Theater an der Wien, Vienna, with the premiere of his Fifth Symphony, Sixth Symphony, Fourth Piano Concerto and Choral Fantasy.

1223.text: Beethoven's Violin Concerto premieres in Vienna.
The opera Hansel and Gretel by Engelbert Humperdinck is first performed.

1224.text: Menotti's Amahl and the Night Visitors premieres on NBC television.
'Silent Night' is first performed in Oberndorf, Austria.
Aida, one of Giuseppe Verdi's most popular operas, made its debut in Cairo, Egypt.

1226.text: Bellini's Norma premieres at La Scala.
Thespis, the first comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, premiered at the Gaiety Theatre in London.
The opera Agrippina, described as George Frideric Handel's first masterpiece, premiered in Venice.

1230.text: Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet ballet premieres in Brno.
